question: How does a developer build an MCP server in Python that serves tools, prompts and resources, and how should each be designed and how is each used by clients?

practices: Do not auto-generate MCP servers from REST APIs; use generation only to bootstrap, then 'aggressively curate' tools, or start from scratch using 'agent stories' (Antipattern Alert).
Design tools as end-to-end actions, not granular composable REST-style ones; keep building blocks as private functions (Designing Tools).
Give tools distinct action names, descriptive but not verbose descriptions, well-defined inputs/outputs, and an underscore-separated namespace prefix to aid tool choice (Designing Tools).
Keep the number of exposed tools reasonable, since LLM tool choice accuracy drops off past soft limits (Designing Tools).
Validate tool inputs, sanitize outputs, add access control and rate limit tool calls (Serving Tools).
Support stdio where possible; use Streamable HTTP for remote servers, which must implement authorization (OAuth); session resumability via SSE event ids is optional (Transports).
Prefer FastMCP over the low-level API for nearly all servers (Why FastMCP?).
Prompts: give direction, specify format, provide examples, evaluate quality across models, divide labor; avoid saying what not to do, use precise descriptions, use separators (Designing Prompts).

Return UserMessage/AssistantMessage objects or document intended use, since applications may place prompts as user, assistant or system content; there is no SystemMessage class (How Prompts Are Used).
Resources: keep them lightweight, with no heavy computation or side effects; descriptions strongly recommended; loading is deferred until read (Exposing Resources).
Use resource templates (URI variables in curly braces) for related resources; the URI is required (Exposing Resources).
